title: Six-view turnaround sheet of one piece at one physical scale
description: A 3x2 sheet of one physical piece, the six wearer-axis views in a fixed order at an identical physical scale, for lampway_image_matte's 3x2 split.

body.subject: One {{piece}}, the same design in every view, exactly as in the first image
body.action: Landscape 3:2, exactly 3 columns by 2 rows, six equal cells with even gutters. Top row FRONT, RIGHT, BACK. Bottom row LEFT, TOP, BOTTOM. These are layout instructions, not printed labels; each view centred in its own cell
body.camera: The wearer's axes: front toward the chest, right from the wearer's own right, back from behind, left from the wearer's own left, top directly down, bottom directly up. IDENTICAL physical scale: one object and one fixed orthographic camera scale rotated around it, never enlarged per cell; short views stay short and end views stay small
body.style: Pure solid #FF00FF including the gutters, identical flat diffuse camera lighting in every cell, matte materials, minimal specular
body.constraints: No merged cells, repeated views, extra views or hero shot; no dividing lines, borders, text or labels

piece.description: the physical piece and its side, e.g. left bracer

reference_image.description: the design authority for this piece

openai/gpt-image*.note: GPT Image wants the reference order stated in prose and takes an explicit size (<= 3840 per edge, ~8.3 MP)

black-forest-labs/*.note: takes resolution + aspect_ratio; tolerates shorter prompts

google/gemini*.note: takes resolution + aspect_ratio; tolerates shorter prompts

sourceful/*.note: Riverflow: flattest albedo; takes resolution + aspect_ratio

gates.description: split 3x2 with lampway_image_matte (cuts and erase rectangles pinned in a recipe), then verify
compare a known cross-view dimension before claiming one scale: equal cells do not prove equal object scale
